about: NET-STD standards register: every protocol, extension, algorithm and format Cerid implements, plans or watches, with its specification and revision, its status in the committed snapshot, its IANA or Cerid codepoints, its owning module and the ROADMAP rows that implement it. A pinned entry (implemented or planned) fails scripts/check-registers.py (the crd-check-registers CTest and repository step) when its draft has expired or its RFC is obsoleted in the snapshot, and every entry fails past its review date. docs/design/registers.md is the contract; COMPLY.0 adds the legal domain in the same format.

snapshot.method: Refreshed on 2026-11-02 by scripts/register-review.py from the approved source plan (72 records; report docs/sessions/2026-11-02-standards-register-light-review.md).

review.cadence: A light scan after each IETF meeting (March, July and November) and a full re-research every year or when a light scan finds a pinned entry's status changed; scripts/register-review.py plans the source reads (a download the user approves), compares them with the register and proposes ROADMAP amendments for the user, never editing rows itself.

entries.note: GREASE values follow the RFC 8701 pattern (0x0A0A, 0x1A1A ... 0xFAFA, the same digit in each ?): reserved as extension identifiers and as version majors, never assigned, and sent by every build, shipping included.

entries.title: Cerid crypto policy generation: signed, monotonic, dated algorithm windows with an offline grace period
entries.note: Names algorithms only by their Cerid algorithm identifiers, so a provider swap or an unverified IANA value never changes a signed artefact. NET.2 issues the first generation and its offline keys.

entries.title: Applying GREASE to TLS extensibility
entries.note: Every build's TLS ClientHello (crd-crypto tls.hpp, the provider's GREASE switched on for every context) carries a reserved value in its cipher suites, supported groups, supported versions and key shares and two reserved extensions, chosen per connection and kept by a ClientHello sent again after a HelloRetryRequest; OpenSSL servers (3.5.9, and since 2026-11-02 4.0.3) ignore them. Cerid's own negotiation sends the same sixteen values (cerid.negotiation).

entries.title: QUIC: a UDP-based multiplexed and secure transport
entries.note: Proven so far in crd-crypto (NET.2): the address-validation tokens of section 8.1 (quic.hpp, decision S13): Retry and NEW_TOKEN tokens told apart by their clear kind (8.1.1), sealed per token under a rotating fleet key and bound to the version, the client's address and, for a Retry token, its port and both connection IDs of its next Initial (8.1.2, 8.1.4, 17.2.5), their lifetimes and the clock skew, and NEW_TOKEN tokens accepted once (8.1.4); the round trips a Retry and a NEW_TOKEN token cost against the amplification limit (section 8) measured with real handshakes. RFC 9000 was read on 2026-11-02 for them. Remaining: the transport itself (4.2a), its paths (NET-PATH) and its qualification against real peers (NET.5).

entries.title: Using TLS to secure QUIC
entries.note: Proven so far in crd-crypto (NET.2): packet protection (section 5, quic.hpp, against the appendix A packets of RFC 9001 and RFC 9369) and the handshake over QUIC (section 4 and 8, QuicHandshake, decision S11): CRYPTO data per encryption level, each level's secrets into packet and header keys, the quic_transport_parameters extension both ways, application protocols required, alerts as CRYPTO_ERROR at their level, no TLS KeyUpdate, tickets under QUIC's own binding; 0-RTT (section 4.6, decision S17): the client's early secret into keys once, tickets allowing 0xffffffff, a server's early data context compared with the ticket's, the server's transport parameters remembered with the ticket and the client's early keys zeroed on a refusal; against OpenSSL's QUIC TLS interface (3.5.9, then 4.0.3) both ways in versions 1 and 2, 0-RTT both ways with the early secrets' probes equal. The 57 codepoint was checked against IANA's TLS ExtensionType Values on 2026-11-01. Address validation (Retry and NEW_TOKEN tokens, RFC 9000 section 8.1) is quic.transport's. Remaining: the transport's use of the keys (key update protocol, discarding keys, the amplification limit) in 4.2a.

entries.title: Low Latency, Low Loss, and Scalable Throughput (L4S) architecture
The Transport Layer Security protocol version 1.3
entries.note: RFC 9846 obsoletes RFC 8446 and keeps version 0x0304 and the wire format; the full re-research of 2026-11-01 maps its technical changes onto NET.2's TLS 1.3 profile (fresh key shares, mandatory key updates before the usage limits, the 2^48-1 epoch bound, general_error, TLS 1.3 only). Proven so far on crd-crypto's TLS records (tls.hpp, decisions S1 to S8): TLS 1.3 only, fresh key shares, general_error toward unauthenticated peers, key updates before the AEAD's usage limit with one request outstanding and the 2^48-1 bound, a peer's user_canceled ignored and its close_notify honoured, against OpenSSL (3.5.9, then 4.0.3) both ways. Tickets and resumption (decision S9): one ticket per connection sealed under a shareable, rotatable ticket key, single-use tickets held in the caller's per-domain store and bound to the context, psk_dhe_ke only with a fresh hybrid share, lifetimes of at most seven days, proven in process and across processes against OpenSSL both ways. Early data (decision S17, sections 2.3, 4.2.10 and 8): off unless both ends configure it, tickets stating their allowance (14,336 bytes over records), single-use tickets through the server's ReplayFilter by their sealed issue time, the provider's 60-second freshness check, early bytes reaching a server's caller only through read_early(), a refused client sending its bytes again after the handshake; proven in process and against OpenSSL 4.0.3 both ways, accepted and refused. The raw UDP record layer remains NET.2's.

entries.title: IANA registry updates for TLS and DTLS: the Recommended column and its discouraged value
entries.note: Every verified codepoint of a TLS registry with the column records IANA's Recommended value (Y, N or D); the review keeps it current and the guard refuses a pinned entry IANA discourages.

entries.title: Post-quantum/traditional hybrid key exchange for TLS 1.3
entries.note: X25519MLKEM768 preferred, SecP384r1MLKEM1024 for high assurance (NET.2). The three groups run inside the provider's TLS stack (crd-crypto tls.hpp); each key share is checked on the wire against the layout (ML-KEM first for X25519MLKEM768, the EC point first for the SecP groups) and every group interoperates with OpenSSL (3.5.9, then 4.0.3) both ways, through a HelloRetryRequest and beside a classical share.

entries.title: Elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman: X25519 and the NIST curves P-256 and P-384
entries.note: The traditional components of the hybrids and the classical-only groups a policy generation refuses by date (first for Cerid services, everywhere by 2030; NET.2 sets the dates). RFC 7748 defines X25519; the NIST curves are FIPS 186-5 and SP 800-186.

entries.title: TLS Encrypted Client Hello
entries.note: Shared mode over the provider's ECH, its HPKE codepoints held by crypto.hpke (crd-crypto tls.hpp, decision S14, docs/design/network-foundation.md#ech): TlsEchKey and its ECHConfig (DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256), HKDF-SHA256 with AES-128-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305), current and previous server keys, a client that never sends a hello without ECH once given a list, retry configurations authenticated by a pinned key and used for one retried connection, ECH disabled and refused told apart, the public name answered only for that recovery, GREASE on every client hello without a list, and the inner hello padded to maximum_name_length; over records and QUIC, against OpenSSL 4.0.3 both ways over records and from a Cerid client over QUIC. RFC 9849 was read on 2026-11-02 and the codepoints checked against its IANA section and IANA's HPKE registry (read 2026-11-02). Its KEM is classical: the inner hello's metadata, never the session keys (the hybrid groups'), would yield to a quantum adversary; a post-quantum HPKE KEM for ECH (ML-KEM-768 0x0041 and X-Wing are in IANA's HPKE registry, draft-ietf-hpke-pq) is adopted once an ECH profile and the providers carry it.

entries.title: TLS certificate compression
entries.note: NET.2 decision S10 (docs/design/network-foundation.md#certificate-compression): a client decodes zstd and zlib through crd-compression into exactly the claimed length, within the 64 KiB a plain Certificate has; a server compresses its Certificate once per context and sends the smallest form only when it is smaller. Brotli (2) is not offered: the engine has no brotli codec.

entries.title: Transport Layer Security (TLS) Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation Extension
entries.note: NET.2 decision S12 (docs/design/network-foundation.md#quic-handshake): a client offers its protocols in its order, a server selects the first of its own that the client offers (section 3.2), and with protocols on either end the two agree or the handshake fails with no_application_protocol (120): a server refuses a client that offers none, a client refuses a server that selects none. Required over QUIC (RFC 9001 section 8.1). A property of the connection, not of the session: tickets do not bind it.

entries.title: HMAC-based extract-and-expand key derivation (HKDF)
entries.note: With SHA-256 and SHA-384 (FIPS 180-4).

entries.title: Hybrid public key encryption (HPKE)
entries.note: Base mode, single shot (crd-crypto hpke.hpp, decision H1, docs/design/network-foundation.md#hpke): DHKEM over X25519, P-256 and P-384 composed from the provider's key agreement and HKDF, with DeriveKeyPair, and the key schedule and AEAD of RFC 9180 section 5, so no HPKE primitive is Cerid's own; proven against every base-mode vector of RFC 9180's test-vectors.json for the KEMs and KDFs in the profile and against the MLS working group's encrypt_with_label vectors. MLS (mls.protocol) and its key packages, paths and Welcome messages are its consumers; the provider's TLS stack keeps its own HPKE for ECH (tls.ech). RFC 9180 was read on 2026-11-02 and the codepoints checked against IANA's HPKE registry (updated 2026-04-16, read 2026-11-02). The post-quantum KEMs, the same key schedule over ML-KEM and the hybrid KEMs, are crypto.hpke-pq.

entries.title: Post-quantum and post-quantum/traditional hybrid KEMs for HPKE
entries.note: crd-crypto hpke.hpp (decisions H1 and H2, docs/design/network-foundation.md#hpke): ML-KEM-768 and ML-KEM-1024 (section 3) and the hybrids MLKEM768-X25519, MLKEM768-P256 and MLKEM1024-P384 (section 4, crypto.hybrid-kems), named by the provider's ML-KEM and hybrid group identifiers, each with SHAKE256's LabeledDerive (draft-ietf-hpke-hpke-03 section 4.4) for DeriveKeyPair and RFC 9180's HKDF key schedule. Proven against every vector of the working group's test-vectors.json at the draft-ietf-hpke-pq-05 tag (hpke-pq-vectors in cmake/pins.json) whose KEM, KDF and AEAD the profile implements; ML-KEM-512 (0x0040, below the policy's ML-KEM-768 floor) and the single-stage SHAKE and TurboSHAKE KDFs (0x0010 to 0x0013, no MLS suite uses them) are outside it. The draft (revision 05, 2026-07-06) and IANA's HPKE registry (updated 2026-04-16, which lists 0x647A as X-Wing, the same construction) were read on 2026-11-02. The post-quantum MLS suites (mls.pq-ciphersuites) consume it.

entries.title: Concrete post-quantum/traditional hybrid KEMs (CG framework)
entries.note: MLKEM768-X25519 (X-Wing), MLKEM768-P256 and MLKEM1024-P384 over the generic CG framework of draft-irtf-cfrg-hybrid-kems-12 (2026-07-06; section 5.5: SHAKE256 as the PRG that expands one 32-byte seed into both halves, SHA3-256 over ss_PQ, ss_T, ct_T, ek_T and the label as the C2PRI combiner), implemented inside crd-crypto's HPKE (crypto.hpke-pq) over the provider's ML-KEM, key agreement and SHA-3 (crypto.sha3). Both drafts were read on 2026-11-02; revision 04's sections 3 and 4, which define the three KEMs, are word for word revision 03's, which draft-ietf-hpke-pq-05 cites. The TLS hybrid groups of tls.hybrid-kex concatenate their secrets instead and are a different construction over the same components.

entries.title: SHA-3 and SHAKE (FIPS 202)
entries.note: SHA3-256 and SHAKE256 through the provider (crd-crypto provider.hpp sha3_256 and shake256): the combiner and PRG of the hybrid KEMs (crypto.hybrid-kems) and the LabeledDerive of the post-quantum HPKE KEMs (crypto.hpke-pq).

entries.title: ML-KEM and hybrid cipher suites for MLS
entries.note: The post-quantum MLS cipher suites (decision M2) over crypto.hpke-pq's KEMs and the provider's ML-DSA (signed purely, empty context, as the draft says). Revision 07 (2026-11-01) was read on 2026-11-02; IANA's MLS registry (updated 2025-11-17) does not list the codepoints yet, so they stay unverified until it does. Planned: the next NET.2 layer adds them to the suite table.

entries.title: Module-lattice-based key-encapsulation mechanism standard (ML-KEM)
entries.note: Private keys are the 64-byte seed d || z; decapsulation rejects implicitly (network foundation P7). The post-quantum half of the hybrid groups (tls.hybrid-kex) and of MLS and HPKE suites.

entries.title: SipHash keyed pseudorandom function
entries.note: SipHash-2-4 (Aumasson and Bernstein, INDOCRYPT 2012) keys every table an adversary can fill (threat T10, network foundation P8); never on the wire.

entries.title: NIST IR 8547: transition to post-quantum cryptography standards
entries.note: Final on 2026-10-27 (the 2024 draft is obsoleted): every quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithm (RSA, ECDSA, EdDSA, finite-field and elliptic-curve DH and MQV), whatever its strength, is deprecated after 2030 and disallowed after 2035; the network foundation's dated refusal of classical-only key exchange follows it.

entries.title: The Messaging Layer Security protocol
entries.note: Cerid's own implementation over crd-crypto's providers (decision M1, docs/design/network-foundation.md#mls), in progress on NET.2. The cipher suites of the profile (decision M2) were checked against RFC 9420 section 17.1 and IANA's MLS registry (updated 2025-11-17, read 2026-11-02); 0x0004 to 0x0006 (X448, Ed448, P-521) are outside it because no provider in the policy implements them.

checklist.mechanism: Every algorithm, group and suite is a register entry with its IANA codepoint; code names the identifier, never a hard-coded choice outside the policy generation.
NET.2 pins the defaults (X25519MLKEM768, SecP384r1MLKEM1024, AES-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305, HKDF, ML-DSA with a classical companion) and every product class implements them.
Signed, monotonic policy generations carry dated migration windows (preferred, accepted only, refused) and a remote signed disable for a broken algorithm.
Version, extension and algorithm negotiation is bound to the handshake transcript, so a downgrade is detected (T05); unknown values are ignored and GREASE keeps the extension points open.
Key sizes follow the pinned groups and the NIST IR 8547 dates; classical-only key exchange is refused first for Cerid services and everywhere by 2030.
Register deprecation dates and generation migration windows are published ahead of time; the offline grace period is bounded.
Post-quantum handshake cost against the amplification limit and the admission budgets is measured, not assumed.
No opportunistic or unauthenticated mode reaches a non-loopback address: every such path is authenticated and encrypted in every build (D4).
